AUTHENTICATED_PARETO_SCHEDULE_V1.claim: compile_schedule accepts a candidate list only if every candidate has a non-empty string id (no duplicates), all nine numeric metrics, and a measurement receipt that is independently verified, carries a 64-hex sha256 and whose subject_sha256 equals sha256 of the canonical JSON of {candidate_id, metrics}; any candidate with non-zero cost_usd_ucb, or an empty list, fails closed with the first offending candidate and reason named. On acceptance it returns the nondominated set (five benefit metrics maximised, four cost metrics minimised, textbook dominance) sorted by id and, for every dominated candidate, the sorted ids of its dominators; it never grants promotion or terminal authority and reports zero credit and zero spend.
scope_limits: NO verification that the receipt sha256 refers to a real measurement; only the binding of metrics to the receipt subject is measured
NO claim about float rounding beyond exact equality of the supplied numbers

CAPABILITY_FIRST_RANKING_V1.claim: Given a list of work items (id, work type, benchmark role, frontier class, new-primitive claim with its proof fields, load-bearing obligation references, exact non-negative leverage and cost numbers) and the number of open checkpoint obligations, rank_work returns every item exactly once, ordered by: eligible work before demoted work; then exact-fraction leverage score (capability + efficiency + reliability) x reuse breadth x generalization x success probability / (wall + compute + memory + complexity cost), descending; then checkpoint audit score (discharge + unlock) x success / wall, which is non-zero only while obligations are open and the item references one; then work id. Benchmark instrumentation without an allowed role, new-primitive claims whose six proof requirements are not all present, and open-world evidence frontier work without a concrete counterexample or verified defect are demoted with score 0. Inputs with an unknown work type, duplicate ids, negative numbers, success probability above 1 or zero total cost on eligible work are refused. The result is planning only: no execution authority and zero acceptance, capability, ownership and terminal credit.
scope_limits: NO shared-residual fan-out tie-break: items never carry shared_residual_cause_ids, so the repository residual ledger is never read
NO live authority reading: checkpoint_open_obligation_count is always supplied; rank_live_work and the current-authority file are out of scope
NO validation of malformed id lists or non-string identifiers beyond what the generator emits

DOCX_EXACT_TEXT_EDIT_V1.claim: Given a .docx package and an exact text-node value that occurs exactly once in word/document.xml, produce a package in which that single text node is replaced and every other package member is byte-identical; when the value occurs zero or several times, fail closed and write nothing.
scope_limits: NO replacement of text spanning several runs or text nodes
NO visual-layout, tracked-changes, comments, headers/footers or numbering guarantees
NO general DOCX editing; one exact text node per call
NO no-op edits: new == old fails closed by design and is outside the input class

DOCX_RUN_SPAN_REPLACE_V1.claim: Given a .docx package and a target string that occurs exactly once (counting overlapping occurrences) in the visible text of the paragraphs of word/document.xml - possibly spanning several runs and text nodes - produce a package whose paragraph texts equal the originals with that single span replaced, with the same number of paragraphs and text nodes and every other member byte-identical; when the target occurs zero or several times, fail closed and write nothing.
scope_limits: NO targets spanning two paragraphs
NO visual-layout, tracked-changes, fields or numbering guarantees
NO headers/footers/footnotes (see DOCX_STORY_PART_REPLACE_V1)
NO general DOCX editing; one span per call

DOCX_STORY_PART_REPLACE_V1.claim: Given a .docx package, a story part name (word/headerN.xml, word/footerN.xml, word/footnotes.xml, word/endnotes.xml or word/comments.xml) and a target string that occurs exactly once (overlapping count) in the paragraph texts of that part, produce a package in which only that part is changed, its paragraph texts equal the originals with the span replaced, and every other member - including word/document.xml even when it contains the same text - is byte-identical; when the part name is not a story part, the part is missing, or the target is absent or repeated inside the part, fail closed and write nothing.
scope_limits: NO body edits through this entry
NO targets spanning two paragraphs
NO creation of missing parts
NO visual-layout, tracked-changes, fields or numbering guarantees

DOCX_TEXT_EDIT_TRANSACTION_V1.claim: Given a .docx package and 1-64 (old,new) edits, apply all of them to word/document.xml atomically: every target must occur exactly once (overlapping count) in the paragraph texts and no two target spans may overlap (touching spans are allowed); then the output paragraph texts equal the originals with every span replaced and every other member is byte-identical. If any target is absent, repeated or overlaps another, or an edit is impossible, fail closed and write nothing.
scope_limits: NO more than 64 edits per call
NO targets spanning two paragraphs
NO headers/footers/footnotes
NO visual-layout, tracked-changes, fields or numbering guarantees

PARETO_FRONTIER_UPDATE_V1.claim: Folding a sequence of candidates into an initially empty frontier with update_pareto_frontier: a candidate without a capability id is refused; a candidate that is not marked reusable, or not independently verified, is not admitted (with the matching reason) and the frontier is unchanged; a candidate with a negative metric is refused; a candidate dominated by an incumbent (no worse on capability, generalization and reliability and on latency, compute, memory and spend, strictly better somewhere, and with the same semantic contract when both declare one) is not admitted and the dominating incumbent is named; otherwise it is admitted, every incumbent it dominates is retired from the active frontier (never deleted, no deletion authority), and the frontier stays sorted by capability id.
scope_limits: NO physical deletion semantics (option_preserving_capability_optimizer is a separate component)
NO claim about order-independence of the final frontier across differing semantic contracts

SACCR_CREDIT_ADDON_V1.claim: Given a portfolio of linear single-name and index credit derivatives, compute the Basel SA-CCR credit asset-class add-on (CRE52.34, 52.48, 52.50, 52.55-52.72) with an explicit intermediate trace per trade.
scope_limits: NO options or CDO tranche deltas
NO replacement cost, PFE multiplier or whole netting-set EAD
NO rating/entity inference from documents; inputs are already structured
entity with mixed supervisory factor or correlation fails closed (ValueError) by design

SAME_IDENTITY_SUPERVISOR_V1.claim: Given a repository root with task manifests (PROJECT_BRAIN_SAME_IDENTITY_TASK_V1), mission files and prerequisite files, and an arbitrary interleaving of choose / claim / execute operations issued by the durable worker identity and by an intruder identity while manifests, missions and prerequisites are edited underneath it, the supervisor (1) chooses only causally-ready tasks (valid manifest for that identity, every prerequisite present and hash-bound, mission file hash-bound, not terminal), highest priority first and smallest task id on ties; (2) lets exactly one identity hold a task lease - a different identity never claims, resumes or executes a leased task and the lease owner never changes; (3) refuses to claim or execute after the manifest or mission drifted from the bound hashes; (4) checkpoints once before the first runtime launch when the manifest asks for it (exit 75, runtime not launched); (5) maps the runtime exit code to COMPLETE (0) / BLOCKED (3,4,5) / FAILED (other) and never launches the runtime again once a task is COMPLETE or FAILED; (6) keeps an append-only, contiguously numbered event log per task and writes one evidence receipt per checkpoint and per runtime attempt.
scope_limits: NO continuous-OBS context validation: instance roots carry no canonical/CANONICAL_POINTER.json and missions carry no continuous_obs block, so continuous_obs_runtime.validate_context is never exercised (separately measurable)
NO real runtime process: the executor is injected and returns scripted exit codes; the default subprocess executor and the ASTRA launcher are out of scope
NO concurrent-process lock contention: operations are sequential in one process; the inter-process claim lock is not measured
NO lease-expiry semantics: lease_seconds is never exceeded inside an instance
NO guarantee about state files written by anything other than the supervisor itself

rule: Rows are written only by execution_guard/true_capability_harness_v1.py from a receipt. A row is a measurement, not a claim; status MEASURED_SANDBOX never counts; status MEASURED_PUBLIC_RUNNER counts only when the receipt is referee-signed.
